title: HUD Expands FHA Financing Eligibility to Qualifying BTR Projects
summary: HUD is expanding FHA financing to qualifying BTR communities, including professionally managed SFRs, duplexes, and triplexes.
body_markdown:
The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) recently announced a significant policy change that expands Federal Housing Administration (FHA) mortgage insurance eligibility to qualifying[build-to-rent (BTR) communities](https://arbor.com/blog/financing-a-build-to-rent-community-through-construction-lease-up-and-stabilization/) . Effective immediately, professionally managed rental developments consisting of detached single-family homes, duplexes, and triplexes are eligible for FHA-insured financing under the same general framework as traditional multifamily properties.


**BTR Communities’ Eligibility**


Under the new guidance, eligible BTR developments may now qualify for:


- [FHA Section 221(d)(4)](https://arbor.com/fha-multifamily/fha-221d4/) : New construction only
- [FHA Section 223(f)](https://arbor.com/fha-multifamily/fha-223f/) : Acquisition or refinancing of recently developed multifamily rental housing only, such as developments with a certificate of occupancy dated less than three years before an application


To qualify, communities must meet requirements that include:


- Operate as a single, cohesive rental property, consisting of at least five units
- Be professionally managed for long-term rental use
- A single tax parcel is preferable, although multiple contiguous parcels on a single site that defines the insured collateral is acceptable
- Projects with a mix of building types that include a BTR component along with traditional multifamily are acceptable


**The Benefits for BTR Developers**


Historically, HUD’s multifamily mortgage insurance programs were largely limited to properties with four or more units, excluding most BTR communities due to their single-family design and subdivision-style layouts. Under the new guidance, HUD recognizes the growth of professionally managed BTR developments and the[increasing demand from renters seeking the space and lifestyle benefits of a single-family home without the barriers to homeownership](https://arbor.com/blog/lifestyle-renters-put-a-new-spin-on-the-american-dream/) .


The announcement creates a new government-backed financing option for a rapidly growing segment of the housing market that could make more projects feasible in a rapidly growing segment of the U.S. rental housing market.


Key benefits include:


- Lower cost of capital
- Higher leverage potential
- Long-term fixed-rate financing
- Reliable access to capital


**BTR-specific Underwriting Considerations**


HUD’s guidance also addresses several BTR-specific underwriting factors, including lease-up timelines, vacancy assumptions, replacement reserves, operating expenses, and sponsor experience. This approach helps ensure FHA financing is structured around the realities of operating a build-to-rent community, and the agency generally expects lenders to use conservative underwriting assumptions that reflect the unique operational characteristics of BTR communities.
